messages.subject: dynamic model with hormonics
parts:
Dear Elias and Ramiro,
Need your assistance in applying the above model using R-INLA.

I want to perfom a per pixel hormonic regression using monthly time series records (single pixel test data is attached)  for NDVI.

I consider,
NDVI_t = NDVI_0 + sum_(i=1 to k) {A_i cos(w_i t) + B_i sin(w_i t)} + e(t)

where e(t) is an error term at time t ,
NDVI_0 represent annual monthly mean,
A_i, B_i and w_i are constants (but unknown),
i is the number of hormonics upto kth hormonic

Ideally,  A and B are coefficients representing amplitude(green-up,  with negative values denoting browning otherwise greening) and phase(NDVI-timing) respectively which is my primary interest.

I came accross the paper on direct fitting of dynamic models in which seasonal dynamic model with hormonics is illustrated in section 3.3.1 but was unable to follow. Also, the model appears to be for time-varying parameters which i think should not be in my case.

Many thanks in advance.

Kind regards,
Erick.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] dynamic model with hormonics
parts:
On Fri, 2015-05-29 at 13:42 +0300, Erick Okuto wrote:


try this code. you can fix the precision in the z-model as you do not
want it to be random

best
H

**********************************************


n = 100
nk = 10
harmonics = matrix(0, n, nk)
for(k in 1:nk) {
harmonics[, k] = sin(pi/n * k * 1:n)
}

beta = matrix(rnorm(nk), nk, 1)
eta = harmonics %*% beta
y = eta + rnorm(n, sd=0.1)

idx = 1:n
formula = (y ~ -1 + f(idx, model="z", Z=harmonics,
hyper = list(prec = list(initial = -4,
fixed=TRUE))))
r = inla(formula,
data = list(y=y, idx=idx, harmonics = harmonics),
family = "gaussian",
control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE))

par(mfrow=c(2, 1))
plot(eta, r$summary.linear.predictor$mean,
xlab = "true", ylab="estimated")
abline(a=0, b=1)
title("linear predictors")
plot(c(beta), r$summary.random$idx$mean[(n+1):(n+nk)],
xlab = "true", ylab="estimated")
abline(a=0, b=1)
title("betas")



--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] dynamic model with hormonics
parts:
Hi Erick,

When you have a model with linear predictor like
  \beta_0 + \beta_1 * covariate_i + random.effect_i
INLA considers both random effect and the fixed effect
  x = {random.effect_i, \beta_0, \beta_1}
with Gaussian prior. The only difference is that the precision for \beta_0 and \beta_1 are fixed. In your case you used a random effect to fit the harmonic coefficients, as like regression coefficients, with fixed precision.

Elias
